title: PCR doubles the DNA every cycle
caption: On a log scale an exponential rise is a straight line: each cycle adds log₁₀ 2 = 0.301. After 10 cycles one copy has become 1,024 (10³); after 30, more than a billion (10⁹).
alt: A straight line of log of the number of copies against cycle number, rising by 0.301 per cycle: 3 at 10 cycles, 6 at 20 and 9 at 30.
description: Copies after n cycles = initial copies × 2ⁿ.
On a log₁₀ axis this is a straight line with gradient 0.301 per cycle.
10 cycles: about 1,000 copies. 20 cycles: about a million. 30 cycles: about a billion.
axisLabels: log₁₀ of copies from one starting molecule
